deepdive.divline: Heavy reinvestment into R&D and new verticals; no dividend signal
deepdive.fin_gap: FY26 results are not yet in the structured financials (Financial Scorecard figures not cleanly parseable).

profile.entities: Digilogic Systems Ltd (parent, TMS); Abhedhya (new subsidiary — RF/radar/EW/comms subsystems); Project UDAN (greenfield manufacturing facility, ~4x current capacity); SBC team (in-house R&D, 8-member)
profile.mgmt: J. Madhusudhan Varma (Chairman & MD, ex-IAF radar veteran, founder); J. Shashank Varma (CEO & WTD, 2nd-gen promoter); Sri Harsha (CFO); hosted by Arkavit Cap Partners (Rajesh Agrawal)
profile.subseg: ATEs (~17% rev); checkout systems (~22%); measurement equipment (~49%); simulators; RF subsystems (new, via Abhedhya); single-board computers (R&D)
profile.themes: Defence indigenization / Atmanirbhar Bharat / Make-in-India; DRDO DcPP (Design-cum-Production Partnership); defence export pull-through (missiles to Philippines, Malaysia, Cambodia)

deepdive.sec: Defence/aerospace test & measurement (ATE / checkout / RADAR test & simulation)

bull_bear.body:
- IPO proceeds (~₹81 cr, Jan-2026) toward growth (UDAN, R&D, RF subsidiary).
- Debt nearly eliminated (D/E 0.04x). Heavy reinvestment into R&D and new verticals; no dividend signal.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Import-supply concentration: most integration hardware imported from US/EU OEMs; geopolitics (Iran, Ukraine) doubled lead times (8 wks → ~4 months) → FY26 ₹22 cr+ spillover and missed guidance. Mitigation claimed via OEM re-routing (1–2% costlier).
- Guidance credibility: missed FY26 guidance, re-issuing same 20–25% band.
- Lumpy, government-budget-dependent order flow; pipeline subject to GoI fund re-prioritization.
- Execution/ramp risk on UDAN and unproven Abhedhya RF vertical (revenue only FY28+).
- Small-base growth lag vs peers (Data Patterns, Zen Technologies).
- SME liquidity/disclosure profile.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident, founder-led, mission-driven; candid on the guidance miss (attributed to import delays, not demand) and on small-base growth criticism. Repeatedly stresses defence growth is "organic," multi-year, cannot be rushed. Personal commitment language from CMD. Maiden call — emphasis on consistent disclosure.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive moat is structural, not technical: once "part-number" nominated in a DcPP production manual, supply is captive — competition only exists at prototyping stage (vs Data Patterns, Zen Technologies).
- OEMs reportedly route ~40% of Asia hardware sales to India — gives Digilogic leverage to get OEMs to fix supply routing.
- Abhedhya kept as a *separate company* deliberately — different talent, infra, pay scales than TMS; RF specialists "cannot sit with" tester/simulator engineers.
- SBC R&D (~1.5–2 yrs old, 8-member team) stays inside Digilogic (not Abhedhya) — baseband control to pair with Abhedhya's RF for full-system ownership.
- ~₹150–160 cr is the implicit revenue ceiling of current facilities — UDAN is the real growth unlock.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

business.body:
- Revenue mix FY26: measurement equipment ~49%, checkouts ~22%, ATEs ~17% (vs ATE+checkout ~44% in FY25 — shift toward higher-margin, software-heavy measurement gear drove margin gain).
- Prototyping ~30% / production ~70% of revenue (prototyping = DRDO; production = defence PSUs like BEL, BDL).
- Per missile program, Digilogic's ATE/checkout scope = ~4–6% of total program budget (e.g. ₹15–24 cr on a ₹300–400 cr program), nomination-based once validated (MSQA-validated).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body:
- EBITDA margin 19.6% (+152 bps), PAT margin 13.3% (+250 bps), driven by software value-add in measurement equipment (low material cost) and product-mix shift.
- Production orders historically deliver "good profitability"; UDAN supplies pre-secured.
latest_quarter.title: Margins

latest_quarter.body:
- Maiden investor call (listed Jan-2026 on BSE-SME); no prior concall — this is the FY26 full-year baseline.
- FY26 vs FY25: revenue +8.4%, EBITDA +16.5%, PAT +33.8%; margins expanded ~150–250 bps; D/E cut 0.4x→0.04x post-IPO.
- Order book fell ₹46 cr → ₹31 cr; pipeline ₹200 cr → ₹110 cr (deferred, not cancelled).
- New disclosures vs IPO doc: subsidiary Abhedhya (RF) formed; Project UDAN timeline (mid-2028); UDAN revenue path FY29–31; SBC R&D; Sperry/Eirad aerospace MOUs; 250-unit spectrum-monitoring order.
- FY26 guidance (20–25%) missed (actual +8.4%) — attributed to import lead-time blowout; same band re-guided for FY27 with Sep-2026 ₹100+ cr PO milestone as proof-point.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- FY27 revenue growth guided **20–25% (also stated 25–30%)** — same band guided (and missed) for FY26.
- Roadmap: target ₹100+ cr of POs in hand by end-Sep-2026 (H1) to underwrite FY27; H1 call to give clarity.
- Current setup can support up to ~₹150–160 cr revenue before needing UDAN.
- Project UDAN incremental revenue: ₹11–13 cr (FY29), ₹28–30 cr (FY30), ₹57–61 cr (FY31).
- Abhedhya (RF subsidiary): no revenue in FY27; first revenue expected FY28.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- Order book ₹31 cr (₹30+ cr by 30-May-2026), executable/billed largely by Aug-2026.
- ₹22 cr+ FY26 spillover carried into first week of April (hardware import delays).
- Pipeline ~₹110 cr (down from ~₹200 cr); shortfall deferred 6–8 months on GoI fund re-prioritization, "not lost."
- Marquee FY26 wins: 4 checkout systems delivered to PSUs; order for **250 units** of deployable spectrum monitoring & analysis systems from a defence PSU.
- Part of ~5–6 main DcPP programs; 4 critical DcPP programs already in production/deployment.
outlook.title: Order book / pipeline

outlook.body:
- DcPP nomination annuities: production orders travel with squadron deliveries to Air Force/Navy/Army.
- Defence-export pull: Indian missile exports (Philippines, Malaysia, Cambodia) carry Digilogic systems (billed via BDL etc.).
- Abhedhya RF vertical (radar/EW/comms subsystems — antennas, up/down converters, exciters) — backward integration to cut reliance on partners.
- In-house SBC (single-board computer) R&D, positioned vs Curtiss-Wright / Abaco, mil-grade −20 to +85°C.
- Aerospace MOUs signed with OEMs Sperry and Eirad to reach Tier-1s (Airbus, Boeing); evaluation phase.
- 2–3 additional new R&D products in pipeline.
outlook.title: Growth drivers

deepdive.thesis: Niche, asset-light defence-electronics play supplying ATEs, checkout systems and measurement/simulation equipment almost entirely to government end-customers (100% B2G ultimately). Edge is the DcPP "nomination" model: once a prototype/tester is validated for a DRDO/PSU program, Digilogic is written into the production manual as the named supplier for that part-number, converting prototyping wins into low-competition, multi-year production annuities. Growth optionality stacked in FY28-31 from (a) Project UDAN manufacturing scale-up and (b) RF subsystem subsidiary Abhedhya moving up the value chain from "tester of systems" to "maker of subsystems."
